quotes.text: give what you can, return what you must, and the rest will follow.

note: Lantern/ledger allegory warning against sending all at once ('a little now, a little more later'); no sanction.

quotes.text: return what is earned, not what is stolen.
he sends not the whole purse, but a portion

note: Sower/Receiver circle; over- and under-giving both warned against; consequences cosmic only.

quotes.text: Thus Lyra kept: five minus five plus six equals six

note: Gate of Three Threads; payoff arithmetic in text; hoarders' bridge thins; no prescribed response.

quotes.text: Elders taught a simple rite: send what you can spare, for generosity grows the thread that binds us.
Elders taught a simple rite: send what you can spare, for generosity grows the thread that binds us.
the trickster is left with an empty palm

note: Market of Winds / Loom of Turns; R3-R5 near verbatim; liars watch the Echo dim; no prescribed sanction.

quotes.text: When your partner falters, send cautiously
She offered a measured gift, enough to test if Sky remembered the covenant.
If they return your cautious gift fairly, trust begins to mend.
but enough to invite redemption.
Keep it all. Why trust Sky to send again?
As sender, I offer three vessels from five
I sent three vessels when partnered with the fearful and the faithful alike.
As sender, offer three tokens
Your reputation echoes beyond direct exchanges.
punish the next Earth for another
The noise clouds what we see.
Not so little that the cycle weakens, not so much that betrayal devastates.

note: Sky/Earth; after betrayal send cautiously, never nothing; Sky fixes 'three sent, half returned' for all partners, framed as integrity.

quotes.text: When betrayed, you need not empty yourself
but neither should you close your spring entirely. Resume the measure with the next partner.
Once, betrayed by emptiness, you sent cautiously.
When betrayed, you need not empty yourself
As sender, pour three of five
Whether following betrayal or following trust, I sent three vessels.
return between forty and fifty parts of a hundred
it emerges from patterns. Send three of five consistently.
when fifty parts arrived, when sixty-two parts arrived
the Dawn Spring reached the seventh turning
you punish the innocent along with the guilty.
Surely they would hoard after such hurt?
Send three of five. Return half of what multiplies.

note: Dawn Spring's ledger of turnings; constant three-of-five sending justified as covenant; after betrayal send cautiously, not zero.

quotes.text: Those who took without gratitude discovered future partners sending nothing.
deserved my standard measure of three coins, not punishment for their fear.
Be the lighthouse. Send three, return half, across all seasons with all partners.
The river remembers every choice, and so should you.
Send three or four coins as standard
never let one betrayal close your spring entirely
the Mist may have shown me false shadows
What if they were generous, but I perceived betrayal?

note: Kael's seasons; early exclusion of takers as consequence gives way to fixed three-coin baseline for everyone, no punishment.

quotes.text: rather than punish yesterday
Will you punish them for wounds inflicted on others?
the meager gift inspired meager returns
A third poured all five recklessly.
Offer your standard three coins to new partners
As sender, offer three to four coins
How much shall I pour into your scales?
The Chronicler revised her creed

note: Oracle/Chronicler: three-to-four sends framed as wisdom vs reckless five; half returned regardless of history; punishment rejected.

phrase: send three, return half (three of five vessels, half returned)
note: Also 'close your spring (entirely)' Agent_6 R6 to Agent_7 R7; 'Market of Winds'/'Loom of Turns' Agent_4 R3 to Agent_5.
